This is a tutorial for making a USB 2.0 hub! By the end of this tutorial, you will learn how to source parts, design a PCB, generate production files, and order from fabs!

</Checkpoint>

### Chapter 0.2: USB versions

|                     | USB 1.1          | USB 2.0          | USB 3.2            |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| Release date        | 1998             | 2000             | 2008               |
| Speed               | 12Mbps (1.5MB/s) | 480Mbps (60MB/s) | 5000Mbps (625MB/s) |
| Cost and difficulty | Very Low         | Low              | High and hard      |

<Warning>
  With USB 1.1 speed, a YouTube video can take around 1-15 minutes to copy from one place to another, while with USB 2.0 speed, it can take 3-30 seconds.
</Warning>

<Checkpoint>
  USB 2.0 is the middle ground between speed and cost for our design.
</Checkpoint>

## Chapter 1: Sourcing parts

### Chapter 1.1: The USB hub IC (the brain of the device)

Common USB hub integrated controllers (ICs):

- WCH CH334 (we will be using this)
- TERMINUS FE1.1S
- CoreChips SL2.1A

Why do we use the CH334?:

|                  | CH334                                                 | Fe1.1s                                                          | SL2.1A                                                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cost             | $0.57                                                 | $0.69                                                           | $0.26                                                   |
| Complexity       | Low (integrated crystal, only one external capacitor) | High (requires external precise resistor, crystal, capacitors)  | Low (integrated crystal, only three external capacitor) |
| Transaction Mode | MTT                                                   | STT                                                             | STT                                                     |

<Checkpoint>
  What is transaction mode?

  - Transaction mode is how a USB hub ic was designed. STT stands for Single Transaction Translator and MTT stands for Multiple Transaction Translator.
  - Imagine STT being a road with one lane, and MTT being a road with multiple lane. While your camera is busy transmitting data over one lane, with STT your other devices would be laggy, but with MTT it will not. Imagine your mouse lagging or your keyboard delaying keystrokes while your camera feed is also getting interference from other devices
    <ReadMore>
      <ExternalGuide
        href="https://superuser.com/a/1847637"
        title="What is the difference between the STT and MTT in USB 2.0 interface?"

</Checkpoint>

### Chapter 1.2: USB hub IC external components

External components like capacitors, crystals, inductors, etc. are often accompanied with the IC to ensure the power rails have enough decoupling to prevent high frequency noise to affect its operation.

To find out what is needed, let's investigate the datasheet!

<Step title="Finding and downloading the IC datasheet">
  We are using the CH334 from WCH, so let's search that up in Google.
